culture.title: Agung Rai Museum of Art
culture.description: A museum, garden and working arts compound in Pengosekan holding the only Walter Spies paintings in Indonesia alongside Balinese classical work.
culture.bonus: Find the Walter Spies room, then sit in the garden and draw something yourself.

culture.title: Pura Taman Ayun, Mengwi
culture.description: The 1634 royal temple of the Mengwi kingdom, a walled garden of multi-tiered meru shrines on an island inside its own moat, and part of Bali's UNESCO listing.
culture.bonus: Walk the full circuit of the moat and count the tiers on the tallest meru.

culture.title: Tanah Lot at Sunset
culture.description: A 16th-century sea temple on a rock stack cut off by every high tide, with the sun setting directly behind it and the surf breaking underneath.
culture.bonus: Time it for low tide so you can walk out across the rocks to the base.

culture.title: Legong at Ubud Palace
culture.description: Legong dancers in gold brocade performing in the courtyard of the royal palace, with a full gamelan orchestra playing a few metres from the front row.
culture.bonus: Watch the dancers' eyes rather than their hands for one whole piece.

culture.title: Purification at Tirta Empul
culture.description: A 10th-century spring temple where Balinese Hindus queue waist-deep to pass under 30 carved water spouts in order, one prayer at a time.
culture.bonus: Actually get in the water and go under every spout in the correct sequence.

culture.title: Neka Art Museum, Ubud
culture.description: The collection Suteja Neka built from 1982 onward, tracing how Balinese painting changed when European artists arrived, in pavilions above the Campuhan valley.
culture.bonus: Find the Lempad drawings and work out what changed in Balinese art after 1930.

culture.title: Kecak Fire Dance at Uluwatu Temple
culture.description: The Ramayana told by a seated choir of 70 men chanting cak-cak-cak with no instruments at all, in a clifftop amphitheatre 70 metres above the ocean, timed to the sunset.
culture.bonus: Sit in the top row and watch how the chorus keeps time without a conductor.

culture.title: Goa Gajah, the Elephant Cave
culture.description: An 11th-century meditation cave with a demon's mouth carved around the entrance, bathing pools excavated in 1954, and a river gorge of Buddhist ruins below it.
culture.bonus: Go down the steps past the pools to the ruined stupa in the gorge, which most people skip.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Most Motorbikes Wins
8ball.description: Walk the length of the street and eat at whichever warung has the most motorbikes parked outside it: no reviews, no menus checked, no exceptions.
8ball.bonus: Order by pointing at what the person ahead of you in the queue is having.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Scooter the Shortcut Blind
8ball.description: Start at Echo Beach, take every left turn you can for 30 minutes without a map, then find your way back. The rice-field lanes behind Canggu are the entire point.
8ball.bonus: Stop at the first roadside stall you pass after the 20-minute mark and buy whatever they sell.

social.title: After Rock at AYANA
social.description: AYANA's late-night room on the Jimbaran clifftop, picking up when Rock Bar below it closes and running DJs until the small hours.
social.bonus: Do Rock Bar for sunset and move up to After Rock the moment it shuts. One night, both.

social.title: Live Band at Laughing Buddha, Ubud
social.description: A small bar on Monkey Forest Road with a mini stage and a band almost every night: blues on Mondays, Latin at the weekend, no cover charge.
social.bonus: Stay for both sets and talk to the band between them.

social.title: Pretty Poison Skate Bowl
social.description: A cocktail bar built around a concrete bowl in the rice paddies, where paid resident skaters session it three nights a week while you drink at the lip.
social.bonus: Stand at the edge of the bowl for a full session without flinching.

social.title: Savaya on the Uluwatu Cliff
social.description: A cliff-edge club 150 metres above the sea that DJ Mag ranks in the world's top five, with international headline sets and an infinity pool on the edge of the drop.
social.bonus: Stay through a full headline set, start to finish, without leaving the floor.

social.title: Deus Ex Machina, Temple of Enthusiasm
social.description: A custom motorcycle workshop in the rice fields that is also a bar, a barber, a gallery and a skate ramp, with live music and bike nights most weeks.
social.bonus: Get a haircut or a shave there before you order the first drink.

social.title: FINNS Beach Club, Berawa
social.description: The biggest beach club in Canggu: bamboo pavilions, several pools, waterslides into the sand and a party zone that runs from lunch to midnight.
social.bonus: Take the waterslide into the pool at least once before you order anything.

social.title: Rock Bar at AYANA, Jimbaran
social.description: A bar built on a rock shelf 14 metres above the Indian Ocean, reached by a cliff-side inclinator, with the spray coming up at you when the swell is big.
social.bonus: Take the inclinator down and get a rail seat on the lowest deck.

social.title: Wednesday Night at Old Man's
social.description: An open-sided beer garden on Batu Bolong beach whose Wednesday night is the single busiest thing that happens in Canggu all week.
social.bonus: Go on a Wednesday or do not go at all. Bare feet, sand still on them.

social.title: CP Lounge, Ubud
social.description: Ubud's late bar: garden seating and tapas at the front, a live band and then a DJ at the back, running to 03:00 in a town that otherwise shuts at ten.
social.bonus: Learn one Latin dance step from a regular on the Friday social night.

social.title: La Favela, Seminyak
social.description: A series of rooms dressed as an overgrown colonial jungle house (antique furniture, vines through the ceiling, Latin music) that turns into a dance floor after midnight.
social.bonus: Find the back room with the dance floor without asking a single member of staff.

social.title: Sunday Session at Single Fin, Uluwatu
social.description: A cliff terrace above the Uluwatu break where Sunday is an institution: DJs and live bands from late afternoon, surfers below, and the sun going down into the Indian Ocean.
social.bonus: Get there by 16:00 for a front-rail seat, and stay for the band after dark.

social.title: Potato Head Beach Club
social.description: The amphitheatre of antique teak shutters on Petitenget beach, open since 2010, with an infinity pool over the sand and a sunset DJ set every evening.
social.bonus: Be in the pool, drink in hand, at the exact moment the sun touches the water.

chill.title: Banjar Hot Springs
chill.description: Three tiers of sulphur pools in the jungle near Lovina, fed through carved stone naga mouths that pour hot water down onto your shoulders.
chill.bonus: Sit under the highest naga spout and take the full weight of the water.

chill.title: Geger Beach, Nusa Dua
chill.description: White sand and reef-flattened turquoise water on the quiet side of Nusa Dua, below a clifftop temple, with seaweed farmers still working the shallows.
chill.bonus: Swim out to the reef edge and float there until you lose track of time.

chill.title: Coffee Tasting at Bali Pulina
chill.description: A hillside coffee and spice plantation north of Ubud where the tasting flight of a dozen coffees and teas is served on a terrace looking across the valley.
chill.bonus: Taste all of the flight, including the ones you are sure you will dislike.

chill.title: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
chill.description: Twelve hectares of banyan forest in the middle of Ubud holding three 14th-century temples, a stone bridge over a ravine and around a thousand long-tailed macaques.
chill.bonus: Find the dragon staircase at the bathing temple in the ravine, not just the main path.

chill.title: Sanur Boardwalk at Dawn
chill.description: Five kilometres of paved seafront path on the east coast, walked before 07:00 when the fishing jukung are coming in and the sun rises straight out of the water.
chill.bonus: Walk the full length one way and get breakfast at the far end before turning back.

chill.title: Pura Ulun Danu Beratan on the Lake
chill.description: The eleven-tiered water temple that appears to float on Lake Beratan, built in 1633 to the goddess of the lake, with mist coming off the water most mornings.
chill.bonus: Get there before 08:00, while the mist is still on the lake and the coaches are not.

chill.title: A Class at The Yoga Barn, Ubud
chill.description: Ubud's original yoga campus: seven studios in a garden running over a hundred drop-in classes a week, from gentle hatha to Friday ecstatic dance.
chill.bonus: Book the class you would normally avoid. Ecstatic dance counts double.

chill.title: Sunset at Batu Bolong Beach
chill.description: Black volcanic sand, a temple on a rock in the surf and a longboard break full of beginners, with the whole of Canggu sitting on the sand at six o'clock.
chill.bonus: Stay on the beach until the light has completely gone, not just until the photo.

chill.title: Massage at Karsa Spa, Ubud
chill.description: A traditional Balinese massage in a timber room set among rice fields and a lotus pond, reached only by walking 30 minutes out along the Campuhan ridge.
chill.bonus: Walk there along the ridge rather than taking a scooter, both ways.

chill.title: Bali Botanic Garden, Bedugul
chill.description: Over 150 hectares of highland garden at 1,250 metres, with an orchid house, a bamboo collection and genuine cool air you will have forgotten existed.
chill.bonus: Find the begonia or orchid house and work out which plants are native to Bali.

foodie.title: Hujan Locale, Ubud
foodie.description: Will Meyrick's modern Indonesian kitchen on the top floor of a colonial-style house in Ubud, cooking regional recipes properly rather than softening them.
foodie.bonus: Order the dish from the region you know least about and ask where it comes from.

foodie.title: Gianyar Night Market
foodie.description: The night market locals drive to from Ubud: babi guling, martabak, satay lilit and sweet jaja cakes down one long street of stalls, at local prices.
foodie.bonus: Eat four things you cannot name before you eat anything you recognise.

foodie.title: Milk & Madu, Berawa
foodie.description: The Canggu breakfast that fuels half the expat population: wood-fired pizza, big plates and good coffee in an open-sided garden on Berawa.
foodie.bonus: Eat breakfast, then stay long enough that it turns into lunch.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Crate Cafe, Canggu
foodie.description: A warehouse of a cafe on the Canggu shortcut, open at 6am for surfers, with smoothie bowls, vegan scrambles and the best-known queue in Bali.
foodie.bonus: Get there before 07:00 and get a table without queueing. That is the whole dare.

foodie.title: Grilled Seafood on the Sand at Menega Cafe
foodie.description: Pick your fish, prawns and clams off the ice at the front, then eat them grilled over coconut husk at a table set directly on Jimbaran sand as the sun drops.
foodie.bonus: Choose the seafood yourself at the counter rather than ordering off the menu.

foodie.title: Nasi Ayam at Ibu Mangku, Kedewatan
foodie.description: One dish, served since 1970: shredded chicken, long beans in grated coconut, a satay stick and a chilli sambal that is genuinely hot, over rice.
foodie.bonus: Eat it with the full sambal, no negotiating it down.

foodie.title: Babi Guling at Ibu Oka, Ubud
foodie.description: Balinese spit-roast suckling pig served on a plate of rice with crackling, blood sausage and sambal, from the warung that made the dish famous outside Bali.
foodie.bonus: Order the special plate with everything on it, crackling and sausage included.

foodie.title: Crispy Duck at Bebek Tepi Sawah
foodie.description: Whole crispy Balinese duck, marinated in island spices and twice-cooked, eaten in a pavilion on the edge of a working rice paddy outside Ubud.
foodie.bonus: Take a paddy-side table rather than an indoor one, even if you have to wait.

foodie.title: Fish Soup at Warung Mak Beng, Sanur
foodie.description: One set meal and nothing else since 1941: crisp fried fish, yellow-spiced fish head soup and rice, served at speed to a room that never empties.
foodie.bonus: Finish the fish head soup, head included. That is the point of the dish.

foodie.title: Babi Guling at Pak Malen, Seminyak
foodie.description: The local's answer to Ibu Oka: a roadside warung on Sunset Road where the suckling pig comes with sharper sambal and half the tourist markup.
foodie.bonus: Order it with extra sambal matah and the crackling on the side.

foodie.title: Pork Ribs at Naughty Nuri's, Ubud
foodie.description: Smoky barbecued pork ribs off a roadside grill, washed down with the martini that made a 1995 warung into an institution.
foodie.bonus: Order the martini. It is shaken at the table and it is stronger than it looks.

foodie.title: Made's Warung, Seminyak
foodie.description: The warung that has been feeding Bali's visitors since 1969, where nasi campur and es campur are served in a courtyard that has outlasted every trend around it.
foodie.bonus: Order the nasi campur, then the es campur for dessert. Both, same sitting.

adventure.title: Uluwatu Cliff Path to Padang Padang
adventure.description: The limestone cliff edge of the Bukit peninsula, walked along the top and then dropped into through a slot in the rock onto the tiny beach at Padang Padang.
adventure.bonus: Squeeze through the rock crevice entrance rather than taking any easier way down.

adventure.title: Sidemen Valley Walk
adventure.description: Terraces, clove trees and palm-sugar tappers in the valley under Mount Agung, walked on village lanes. The Bali people claim Ubud used to be.
adventure.bonus: Buy palm wine straight from someone who tapped it that morning.

adventure.title: Cycle the Jatiluwih Rice Terraces
adventure.description: A UNESCO-listed valley of terraces under Mount Batukaru, far bigger and emptier than Tegallalang, with a lane system you can ride for hours.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full green loop and find the temple at the top end of the valley.

adventure.title: Bali Treetop Adventure Park
adventure.description: Seven high-ropes circuits strung between trees up to 20 metres off the ground, inside the cool highland botanical garden at Bedugul.
adventure.bonus: Complete the hardest circuit on offer, including the Tarzan jump.

adventure.title: Mount Batukaru Jungle Trek
adventure.description: Bali's second-highest mountain, climbed from a mossy temple through genuine cloud forest with no crowds at all, which is the opposite of the Batur experience.
adventure.bonus: Do the whole climb without a single stop longer than five minutes.

adventure.title: Snorkel the USAT Liberty Wreck at Tulamben
adventure.description: A torpedoed American cargo ship lying in 5 to 30 metres of water 30 metres off a black pebble beach, so encrusted with coral you can snorkel it without a tank.
adventure.bonus: Free-dive down to the ship's ribs at least once, no tank, no excuses.

adventure.title: Munduk Waterfall Circuit
adventure.description: Three waterfalls linked by a coffee-and-clove plantation path in the cool highlands above the twin lakes, at 800 metres where the air finally drops below warm.
adventure.bonus: Walk between all three falls rather than driving to each car park.

adventure.title: Waterbom Bali
adventure.description: A water park built into five hectares of tropical garden in Kuta, running since 1993, with a near-vertical Climax drop capsule that opens the floor under you.
adventure.bonus: Do the Climax capsule first, before you have time to think about it.

adventure.title: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
adventure.description: The steep amphitheatre of terraces north of Ubud, farmed on the thousand-year-old subak water-sharing system, walked properly from the valley floor rather than photographed from the road.
adventure.bonus: Walk right down into the valley and back up the far side, not just the top path.

adventure.title: Campuhan Ridge Walk at First Light
adventure.description: A paved spine of ridge above two rivers, walked out of Ubud before the heat, with elephant grass either side and nothing but roosters for noise.
adventure.bonus: Walk out to Karsa Kafe at the far end rather than turning back at the halfway point.

adventure.title: Surf Lesson at Kuta Beach with Odysseys
adventure.description: A first surf lesson on the long sand-bottomed beach break where most of Bali learns, with a two-hour session timed to the day's tide.
adventure.bonus: Stand up and ride one wave all the way to the sand before the lesson ends.

adventure.title: Tukad Cepung Waterfall
adventure.description: A waterfall inside a cave, where the roof has collapsed just enough to let a single shaft of light down onto the water in the middle of the morning.
adventure.bonus: Be standing under the light shaft between 09:00 and 11:00, when it actually appears.

adventure.title: Ayung River Rafting with Sobek
adventure.description: Eleven kilometres of class II–III water through a jungle gorge below Ubud, past carved rock reliefs cut into the canyon wall, with the island's oldest rafting outfit.
adventure.bonus: Take the front seat of the raft and stay in it for the whole run.

adventure.title: Kelingking Beach on Nusa Penida
adventure.description: The T-Rex headland on Nusa Penida, with a near-vertical bamboo-railed descent of 400 metres down the spine to a beach almost nobody actually reaches.
adventure.bonus: Go all the way down to the sand, not just to the viewpoint, and climb back up.

adventure.title: Sekumpul Waterfall Trek
adventure.description: Seven separate falls dropping into one jungle gorge in the north, reached by several hundred steps down and a river crossing at the bottom.
adventure.bonus: Get into the plunge pool at the base of the tallest fall, however cold it is.

adventure.title: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
adventure.description: A 02:00 start and a two-hour climb up an active volcano, so you are on the 1,717-metre rim when the sun comes up over Mount Agung and the caldera lake below.
adventure.bonus: Have your breakfast egg steamed in a volcanic vent at the summit.
